assertions: Sir William Waller overcomes: Waller's Parliamentarian army wins the engagement near Alresford/Cheriton on the day asked, 29 March 1644
Sir Ralph Hopton and the Royalist side are defeated and forced to give ground/retreat, not Waller
Hopton has no ready supplies or effective assistance forthcoming: only Mars and the South Node in the 9th, his side is unsupported
Waller's assistance and substance are strong and present: the Sun, lord of Waller's substance/assistants, is in the 10th in the very degree of his exaltation (19° Aries)

Waller's fortune is swift and growing: Moon in her exaltation with Jupiter, swift and increasing in light, applying toward Venus/Jupiter party significators (Ascendant, Moon, Jupiter and Venus for Waller)

Hopton's significator Saturn is wholly debilitated — sub radiis, in his fall, peregrine, in no aspect to any planet, and square the cusp of the 7th — so Hopton cannot sustain the fight or recover the day
method: Lilly horary astrology (classical whole-sign/essential dignity): 1st-house party vs 7th-house opponent significators
reasoning: Waller side taken by Ascendant and Moon, Jupiter and Venus: Moon exalted and with Jupiter, swift and increasing in light; Sun lord of Waller's 2nd/substance in 10th at 19° Aries, exact exaltation degree — strong, elevated, assisted. Hopton side by Saturn lord of 7th: Saturn sub radiis, in fall, peregrine, unaspected, square 7th cusp — debilitated and isolated; 9th holding only Mars and South Node shows no supplies ready for him. Essential and accidental strength is entirely on Waller's side, so Waller overcomes, and the figure was erected the day of engagement so outcome is that same day.
summary: Waller should overcome and Hopton be defeated in the Cheriton engagement on 29 March 1644.
